blogPosts.title: Images hosted on redacted.sh
blogPosts.bbBody:
As of yesterday, uploads that uploaded with an album cover on Redacted (such as the latest from https://orpheus.network/torrents.php?id=1644328 – the most recent upload as of writing) now display correctly on Orpheus. All previous uploads with a redacted.sh image also render as expected. 

This is handled by redirecting the image url back to orpheus.network where an API call is made to Redacted to download the source image, and then it is cached locally. Subsequent page views fetch the image from the cache and do not send further traffic to Redacted.

It is therefore unnecessary to rehost redacted.sh images elsewhere (which of course was always the case).

I would like to extend my warmest thanks to Redacted staff (especially Fibonacci for being available to answer the various questions I had) for allowing us to do this.

blogPosts.title: Dolly Parton – Celebrating the Many Sides of a Country Legend
blogPosts.bbBody:
[align=center][size=4][url=https://orpheus.network/torrents.php?id=58698]Dolly Parton – The Essential Dolly Parton (2005)[/url][/size]
[b](Anthology) (Country, Folk, Blues, Rock, Pop)[/b]

[url=https://orpheus.network/torrents.php?id=58698][img]https://i.ibb.co/6cjLxJVw/81vzkn3nk-OL-SL1500.jpg[/img][/url][/align]

In celebration of Dolly Parton’s remarkable career, we’re featuring The Essential Dolly Parton, a collection that brings together songs from nearly four decades of her music.

Released in 2005, the two-disc anthology covers a wide range of Dolly’s work, from her early country recordings through her biggest hits and later career. It includes many of the songs that have become closely associated with her, including “Coat of Many Colors,” “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You,” “Here You Come Again,” and “9 to 5.”

For anyone discovering Dolly Parton for the first time, The Essential Dolly Parton is a great place to start. It shows the range of her songwriting and her ability to tell stories about love, heartbreak, family, hardship, and everyday life, while also showing how naturally she moved between traditional country and more mainstream music.

Taken together, these songs offer a good picture of what has made Dolly Parton such an enduring figure in American music: a distinctive voice, a gift for songwriting, and a talent for making even very personal stories feel universal.

blogPosts.title: email delivery problems [updated]
blogPosts.bbBody:
Just a heads-up, we are experiencing email delivery issues to several email providers, most importantly Proton Mail. This mostly impacts invites and password reset emails.

Unfortunately, there is nothing we can do to resolve the issue from our side. Spamhaus decided to add our domain to their blocklist for no apparent reason and is neither providing any information for doing so, nor showing any willingness to remove the bogus entry.

Some email providers, among them Proton Mail, blindly reject emails listed on the Spamhaus blocklist, hence preventing us from sending emails to a lot of our users.

It's unfortunate that a service such as Spamhaus abuses their power to undermine net neutrality under the guise of assisting people worldwide and offering free spam blocking services. Their refusal to respond to our removal requests in any sensible way shows that this organization is not committed to "making the internet a better place", as they claim, instead pushing the internet towards centralization and censorship. It's unclear whether they are just incompetent or covertly malicious, but clearly they do not exercise their power responsibly.

Until Spamhaus reverses their decision, or Proton Mail revisits their blind trust in Spamhaus's flawed service, there is not much we can do, other than recommend you to avoid both of them, or voice your concerns towards them yourself. I'd like to stress that Proton is not the only affected email provider, but by a far margin the most popular affected one among our users.

[b][color=red]UPDATE:[/color][/b] Spamhaus has removed our listing, as arbitrarily as they added it. Email delivery to Proton and other email providers is restored for the moment. Let us hope it will stay at that.

blogPosts.title: What a long, strange trip it’s been — celebrate Bob Weir’s music and legacy with American Beauty
blogPosts.bbBody:
[align=center][size=4][url=https://orpheus.network/torrents.php?id=7627]Grateful Dead – American Beauty (1970)[/url][/size]
[b](Album) (Folk Rock, Psychedelic, Bluegrass)[/b]

[url=https://orpheus.network/torrents.php?id=7627][img]https://i.ibb.co/4RM6xzCC/a-HR0c-HM6-Ly9wd-HBpb-Wcub-WUv-MTcy-Zj-Ay-Lmpw-Zw.jpg[/img][/url][/align]

In recognition of the recent passing of Bob Weir, co-founder, vocalist, and rhythm guitarist of the Grateful Dead, we’re featuring American Beauty, an album that highlights his essential role in the band’s sound and spirit.

Released in 1970, American Beauty presents the Grateful Dead at their most intimate, blending folk, country, and rock with rich harmonies and timeless songwriting. Weir’s voice is a key presence on the album, most prominently on “Sugar Magnolia” and “Truckin’,” and also throughout in the shared vocals and interplay that define the Grateful Dead’s collaborative approach.

For anyone discovering the Grateful Dead for the first time, American Beauty offers clarity, heart, and warmth. Concise, melodic, and inviting, it captures the band’s collaborative spirit and Bob Weir’s distinctive contributions, a blend of melody, groove, and storytelling that defines what makes the Dead so enduring and continues to draw new listeners in decades later.

blogPosts.title: The plaintext announcement announcement
blogPosts.bbBody:
A quick update on an upcoming change that will have an impact on seeding at Orpheus.

As [url=forums.php?action=viewthread&threadid=23964]announced at the beginning of this year[/url], in the interest of security for everyone, we are turning off plaintext announcements to the tracker. Since that time, if you have plaintext configured, the settings page displays the following message:
[quote][important]WARNING: your announce url uses the plaintext http protocol!
This functionality will be retired on 2025-07-01 (a.k.a very soon).[/important][/quote]
Most people have updated their configurations, and for this, staff are grateful as it will cut down on support during the transition period.

With the upcoming server change, if you have a torrent with an announce url that begins with [code]http://home.opsfet.ch[/code], it will begin to receive timeout errors because the tracker will no longer listen on the http plaintext port (port 80). The url must be changed from [code]http[/code] to [b][code]https[/code][/b]. You do not need to download the torrent file again, it may be edited in place.

See [[announcechange]] for details on how to change announce urls.
blogPosts.body:
A quick update on an upcoming change that will have an impact on seeding at Orpheus.

As announced at the beginning of this year, in the interest of security for everyone, we are turning off plaintext announcements to the tracker. Since that time, if you have plaintext configured, the settings page displays the following message:
WARNING: your announce url uses the plaintext http protocol!
This functionality will be retired on 2025-07-01 (a.k.a very soon).

Most people have updated their configurations, and for this, staff are grateful as it will cut down on support during the transition period.

With the upcoming server change, if you have a torrent with an announce url that begins with 
http://home.opsfet.ch
, it will begin to receive timeout errors because the tracker will no longer listen on the http plaintext port (port 80). The url must be changed from 
http
 to 
https
. You do not need to download the torrent file again, it may be edited in place.

See Wiki › FAQ ~ How do I change the announce URL in all my torrents? for details on how to change announce urls.

blogPosts.title: A most unfortunate set of circumstances
blogPosts.bbBody:
People who were online yesterday received the surprise of seeing various sensitive site configuration values in place of the expected website. How that happened was a perfect storm of circumstances, that have been addressed to avoid it from happening in the future, and all the exposed values have been rotated. [b]No user data was at risk at any time.[/b]

Here is the post mortem of the incident.

To understand it all, we have to go back a number of years and begin with the original what.cd Gazelle codebase. The architecture for setting up configuration variables back then was rather cumbersome and awkward to maintain. As I recall, it was a plain text file of key/value pairs and it was quite easy to make errors when making changes. And it probably meant that a lot of developers who worked on Gazelle at the time found it easier to just hard-wire the number they needed, where they needed it, rather than make them easy to reconfigure.

One of the changes we made years ago was to change the configuration data to a PHP file, so that the interpreter would catch errors as soon as it was loaded. If there was an error, the site would show a white screen of death. After this, it became easy to pull out a lot of magic numbers from the code and turn into (documented!) configuration variables.

The next problem encountered was that it was cumbersome to keep separate the default values required to bring up a site, and the values a specific site needs (like database passwords). Another change was made to address this, in that the default configuration file would be "good enough" for most needs, here or elsewhere, and only a small number of variables would need to be overridden to tailor behavior for any given site.

Fast forward to a third issue we ran into, where a misconfiguration on the front end proxy would dump the PHP code of the main page of the site. So that part of the site was also revamped to show only [code]require gazelle.php;[/code] on a page if something went wrong.

And then we get to a fourth problem. In revamping that code, I ran into what I had remembered as being a termed a Gate Problem, which, in the literature, goes by the name of a Chesterston Fence.

G. K. Chesterton was a philosopher and in regards to the economics of political reform, formulated the following parable:
[quote]There exists in such a case a certain institution or law; let us say, for the sake of simplicity, a fence or gate erected across a road. The more modern type of reformer goes gaily up to it and says, “I don’t see the use of this; let us clear it away.” To which the more intelligent type of reformer will do well to answer: “If you don’t see the use of it, I certainly won’t let you clear it away. Go away and think. Then, when you can come back and tell me that you do see the use of it, I may allow you to destroy it.”[/quote]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In relation to Gazelle, there was a pair of statements at the beginning and end of a large section of code that had the effect of saying "if anything wants to output stuff to the page in this section... just throw it away". And when I refactored the code, I did not think hard enough about its use and how anything could like that could happen, and removed the two statements.

And then there is a final situation that was needed to align with the rest, the blame of which belongs to PHP itself. PHP is a funny language, in that, by default, it assumes somewhat paradoxically that a file you want it to execute does not contain any PHP code. It assumes the file is text, perhaps HTML, and must be sent to the browser. To instruct PHP that, yes, there is actually PHP code to interpret, the source code file must contain "<?php" From that point on, the PHP interpreter will interpret the rest of the file as php code. No other language behaves this way.

And finally we get to yesterday. I was working on a merge request in the CI which will change the names of a couple of configuration variables in the override file. As I looked them up, I noticed an old key belonging to retired code that no longer serves any purpose. So I deleted it, as there is no point keeping obsolete code present.

And this is where we get to the crux of the matter. I was working in the CI and not looking at the site, and for reasons I will never fathom, I managed to move to the top of the file and repeat the operation, deleting the first line. After that, first line no longer had the opening "<?php" and the interpreter faithfully dumped it to the browser, which I missed completely.

And as a result, a series of sensitive configurations were posted at the top of the page. Sensitive in that yes, if one had access to the server, you could log into the database and exfiltrate any amount of data. But there was never any risk of that. The backend server is so heavily firewalled off that even if you knew the server address, scanning it would reveal no open services, no means of purchase to get inside. There were also some internal network addresses that reveal little, and some other minor things like exact ids of wiki pages. Since then, all of the sensitive values have been reset to new values. At no time was any personal data like email addresses or announce keys ever in danger of being exposed. And yes, the bit of code that loads the configuration file now has the safeguard code back in place to prevent it from ever again being spewed out by accident.

The biggest visible consequence of this (apart from having to log in anew) is that we have pushed forward with the planned changes to RSS feeds. Now you will definitely need to update your feed addresses to get new data, as the internal signature key value was changed and the old URLs no longer work.

And so all of that is why we took the site down: to change what needed to be changed, and update what needed to be updated. My humble apologies. This, at least, will not happen again.

Now you will definitely need to update your feed addresses to get new data, as the internal signature key value was changed and the old URLs no longer work.

And so all of that is why we took the site down: to change what needed to be changed, and update what needed to be updated. My humble apologies. This, at least, will not happen again.

blogPosts.title: Upload stat adjustment for users affected by the peer scraping / ghostleeching event
blogPosts.bbBody:
Following the recent [thread]22288[/thread] we have adjusted the upload stats of all users who gained excess upload due to the subsequent ghostleeching. This was mostly necessary due to users not changing their client IP or port, as recommended in the thread above.

We identified 2,061 affected users, removing a total of 209 TiB illegitimate upload, with a median adjustment of 26 GiB.

If any affected user has good reason to assume they lost significant amounts of legitimate upload by this adjustment please reach out by sending a https://orpheus.network/staffpm.php with details and we will review your data. To prevent our staff team from being overloaded, messages that fail to provide a verifiable reason will not be handled.

All affected users have received a PM with details about their individual adjustment.

blogPosts.title: Unintended server maintenance
blogPosts.bbBody:
You may have noticed the site was down for several hours. This follows a database modification that went wrong. #blamespine

The database was restored from the latest backup, which was completed around 04H00 UTC. Unfortunately, all torrents that were uploaded after exactly 2024-04-27 04:13:48 until the outage, which took place about six hours later, are no longer.

In other words any torrent id greater than 2652584 is no longer present. I can offer some meager consolation in that bonus points awarded for uploads has been kept.

All other information in the database is intact (such as forum posts and private messages).

Sincere expressions of regret.

blogPosts.title: Monero donations
blogPosts.bbBody:
Due to [url=https://orpheus.network/forums.php?action=viewthread&threadid=7185]popular demand[/url] we now accept Monero (XMR) donations in addition to Bitcoin.

Monero is a cryptocurrency focusing on anonymity, with some strong, inherent guarantees. Another plus are the low transaction fees. With bitcoin we (or rather, you) have been facing fees of $0.70 and more for a simple transaction in the past weeks (see https://mempool.space/ to gauge the current fees). Monero transaction fees range around $0.01.

If you want to donate monero, you can find your personalised donation address at https://orpheus.network/donate.php

A word of warning however: [b]do not send[/b] monero directly [b]from an exchange[/b] or similar service. Transfer to your own wallet before. The donation address can be linked to Orpheus. If you want or need to send directly from an exchange please use bitcoin for your own good.

[b]A big Thank You to all past and future donors who help to keep this site alive![/b]

blogPosts.title: Vulnerability in qBittorrent 4.5.1
blogPosts.bbBody:
If you have enabled the web interface on qBittorrent 4.5.1 Windows, and the machine is accessible directly over internet, you are vulnerable.  If an attacker can guess the name of a file in a specific folder on your computer, then they can view and copy it.

The long and the short of it: [b]deactivate the Web UI[/b] pending the release of an update. It is probably not as bad as it seems: if you are exposing a Windows machine directly to the net, you probably have bigger problems than this ;-)

The report is here:
https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/issues/18618

blogPosts.title: Contest payout soon
blogPosts.bbBody:
A brief update on the situation.

Following the late change to the rules – uploads must be seeded (by someone, not necessarily the uploader), the task that drains stale announces has been modified. The aim is to help those people who are not in a position to seed 24/7.

Before, when your client stopped announcing it is seeding a torrent (i.e. you stopped it), the information was drained from the database 6 hours later via a scheduled task. Now, this interval is configurable, and was set late Friday/early Saturday to the current value of 78 hours (3 days, 6 hours).

This will be sufficient to catch those people who are able to seed only on weekends. I will continue to let things run as they are for another 24 hours to allow people who can only seed during the week to restart their clients. The contest will be paid out about 24 hours from now.

Also note, the sale in the bonus shop has ended. Most people will win so many bonus points that it will not make much of a difference.
